newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgaria lev firms to dollar, closes flat to mark.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria lev firms to dollar, closes flat to mark.

text.p: The Bulgarian lev closed between 994-995.50 per mark, unchanged from opening levels in thin interbank trade, dealers said.
* The lev gained to 1,738-1,743 per dollar from the morning's 1,741-1,745.
* Dealers said there was active mark/dollar arbitrage between banks and exchange bureaux where banks bought relatively cheap dollars for marks, which were later channeled to international markets.
The arbitrage occurred around 1.7430/50 marks per dollar.

* Companies and individuals were seen actively exchanging foreign currency savings into levs after the lev was pegged at 1,000 per mark under an IMF-prescribed fixed exchange rate system, known as a currency board, traders said.
* People were selling mainly dollars as the bulk of the foreign currency savings are dollar-denominated.

* Dealers expect the lev to trade near or firmer than the 995 levs-per-mark bid of the central bank in the next few months due to the traditionally larger foreign currency supply in the summer season.
* Under the currency board arrangement introduced on Tuesday the central bank pledged to buy and sell an unlimited amount of marks at fixed rates of 995 levs per mark bid and 1,000 levs ask.
